The Federal Government on Wednesday announced that it has secured the establishment of the first-ever Media and Information Literacy Centre in Nigeria to tackle fake news, misinformation and disinformation. The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Idris Mohammed, disclosed this while addressing participants at the Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum in Abuja. Mohammed said the centre, a UNESCO Category II institute, was part of Nigeria’s efforts to strengthen information credibility, promote media literacy and improve public understanding of government policies. The minister said the government recognised that effective communication went beyond announcing policies and explaining decisions, stressing the need for dialogue, citizens’ participation and public confidence. He said, “In Nigeria, we have also taken a step further by applying for, bidding, and also clinching the first ever Media and Information Literacy Centre, and it’s a UNESCO Category II institute here in Abuja.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Now this is the contribution that Nigeria is doing to help tackle the menace of fake news, misinformation, and disinformation.” According to him, the traditional approach in which leaders simply disseminated information for citizens to consume without feedback is no longer tenable in an era of rapidly evolving communication technology. “Government communication must go beyond announcing policies or explaining decisions. It also has to do with encouraging dialogue and building public confidence. “Gone are the days when leaders are expected to just dish out information to citizens, and citizens are expected to swallow and consume this information without any feedback. Today communication has become very, very sophisticated, especially with the role that technology is playing,” he said. The minister said the administration of President Bola Tinubu prioritised transparent communication, citizens’ engagement and national values as tools for promoting national unity and social cohesion. He noted that the government worked with the media and civil society organisations while embracing technology to strengthen public communication. Idris, however, stressed the need to protect the credibility of information even as governments and institutions adapted to technological developments. He said, “As Minister of Information and National Orientation, just as the role that my colleagues on the aforementioned are also doing, it is our responsibility to deepen cooperation on information, on media literacy, and in crisis communication.” The minister described the establishment of the UNESCO Category II Media and Information Literacy Centre in Abuja as “Nigeria’s contribution to the global fight against false information.” He said the initiative would strengthen efforts to address the growing threats posed by fake news, misinformation and disinformation. Idris also urged participants from 126 countries attending the forum to explore opportunities in Nigeria, assuring them that the country remained open to international partnerships and engagement.
